title.value: Measuring Commonality in Recommendation of Cultural Content: Recommender Systems to Enhance Cultural Citizenship
title.justification: The title explicitly states the focus of the paper, which is on measuring commonality in the recommendation of cultural content and its implications for cultural citizenship.
title.quote: Measuring Commonality in Recommendation of Cultural Content: Recommender Systems to Enhance Cultural Citizenship

extractions.description: This paper introduces the concept of 'commonality' as a metric to evaluate recommender systems in cultural content distribution. Focused on cultural citizenship, it proposes a shift from personalization to enhancing shared cultural experiences and diversity. The study includes a case analysis of movie recommendations, comparing traditional and commonality metrics, highlighting the complementarity of these approaches and advocating for diversity and commonality in the media.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily addresses cultural citizenship and the design of recommender systems to promote cultural diversity and shared cultural experiences. While these are important social considerations, they do not explicitly align with the core themes of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We advocate for the design of recommender systems delivering cultural content to be motivated not only by personalization–or associated commercial interests–but also by appropriate normative principles.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus on cultural diversity and citizenship through recommender systems does not directly relate to any predefined category of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: In this way, commonality contributes to a growing body of scholarship developing ‘public good’ rationales for digital media and machine learning systems.

primary_sub_category.justification: The detailed study of recommender systems and cultural content does not correlate with any specific sub-category under the given Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development frameworks.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our proposed commonality metric responds to a set of arguments developed through an interdisciplinary dialogue between researchers in computer science and the social sciences and humanities.

new_primary_category.value: Digital Media for Social and Cultural Development
new_primary_category.justification: The paper introduces new insights and metrics for digital media systems that enhance cultural citizenship, a concept not covered by existing sustainable development categories related to climate or ecology.
new_primary_category.quote: This paper introduces commonality as a new measure of recommender systems that reflects the degree to which recommendations familiarize a given user population with specified categories of cultural content.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The specific focus on recommender systems as tools for enhancing cultural citizenship and diversity is a novel area not covered in the existing list of sub-categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we introduce commonality as a new measure of recommender systems that reflects the degree to which recommendations familiarize a given user population with specified categories of cultural content.
